1160	And it came to pass one day, that despite all this, one of
1161	the sons, who brought Father tefillin,
1162	it became clear at the last moment that they were Rabbeinu Tam's, and he took them off at the last moment because of Father's question.
1163	And indeed Father caught it at the last moment, did not make the blessing, and they replaced them for him with Rashi's before Rabbeinu Tam's.
1164	But there was a somewhat more inward incident than this, that on one of the occasions
1165	the son had already grown used to this question, and answered automatically, "Yes, yes, it's Rashi, yes, yes, it's Rabbeinu Tam."
1166	A mistake came out, and Father made the blessing on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1167	And afterward: "Oy, what have I done?"
1168	The son came and apologized.
1169	Then came the consolations: it is written in the holy books that every person will experience
1170	once in his life that he errs and makes the blessing on Rabbeinu Tam's,
1171	before Rashi's. Once in his life it will happen to him, as brought in the book Taamei HaMinhagim, which says,
1172	a tradition from holy men: the man who is careful all his days to put on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin and never lacks it
1173	all his days through any constraint, must be made to err once and make the blessings on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin
1174	and pray in them.
1175	He also brings there from the book Yakar Tosefta, written by a kabbalist according to Rav Mordechai of Dubrovna,
1176	that Rabbeinu Tam arranged in the heavenly court that whoever puts on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin will at least once
1177	in his life err and put on, with a blessing, Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin instead of Rashi's tefillin.
1178	And that there is such a tradition in the name of the holy Rav of Lublin, and afterward he brings further books there, and more.
1179	In any case, for our purposes, even the mistake that happened to my father was done by deliberate providence
1180	from Heaven, because that is how it had to be, since Rabbeinu Tam asked in Heaven that whoever he may be,
1181	once he will come to a mistake,
1182	so that he will get to bless and pray with Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1183	But our father was meticulous, very meticulous, between man and his fellow, between man
1184	and God, especially in monetary matters.
1185	For several years he would receive a calendar in the mail, the calendar
1186	of the Or HaChaim yeshiva in Jerusalem; they sent it to him by mail every year.
1187	Right away our father would sit down, that very day he would sit down, and send them back
1188	an envelope with payment. Once we asked him:
1189	Why do they send it to you, and why do you pay for what you never even asked for, when we already have a calendar
1190	at home? He answered that apparently once I donated to them,
1191	and since then they send it to me regularly, and since they take the trouble to send and also enclose an envelope
1192	for return payment, they expect to receive, so I do not change from what I did
1193	at the beginning, the first time. And therefore he continued to pay for the calendar although he owed them nothing, he had not asked
1194	that they send it to him again, but if they already send it and have grown used to it, then I too continue
1195	in what I did the first time. Care in monetary matters, care
1196	in his own monetary matters, regarding what belongs to another, yes?
1197	A person is called a tzaddik when he is careful in monetary matters; "Noach ish tzaddik."
1198	Chazal tell us, the Gemara says, a tzaddik in money.
1199	As we produced a comprehensive shiur on the subject, called "Ish Tzaddik."
